record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: In VSe2/MoS2 heterostructures, how are V-atom spins and defect-induced spins in VSe2 and MoS2 coupled at the interface, does work-function-driven charge redistribution and Schottky-barrier formation enhance the exchange-bias effect, and can the effect be tuned by changing MoS2 thickness, Se-vacancy concentration in VSe2, or by replacing VSe2 with other defect-magnetic transition-metal dichalcogenides such as WSe2 or TiSe2?

evidence.quote: Nonetheless, several questions remain to be answered. For instance, it is unclear how spins of V atoms and spins induced by defects (Se vacancies) are coupled to MoS2 spins (either Mo- or S-vacancy induced) at VSe2/MoS2 interfaces and contribute to the EB effect.

The accumulation of electrons in the VSe2 layer could give rise to the enhanced ferromagnetism in this layer and, hence, contributes to the change in net magnetization of the VSe2/MoS2 heterostructure and hence the observed EB effect. Further studies are needed to verify this hypothesis.

It would also be interesting to investigate how the interfacial magnetism and EB behavior in the VSe2/MoS2 heterostructure are altered when the thickness of the MoS2 film is reduced to a few layers or the monolayer limit.

Since the net magnetization of the VSe2 film can be tuned by controlling Se-vacancy concentration [109], it would also be interesting to examine if the EB field of the VSe2/MoS2 heterostructure could be tuned by varying the magnetization of the VSe2 layer.

Given the fact that other TMDs, such as Se-deficient WSe2 and TiSe2 monolayers, could exhibit ferromagnetic ordering even at room temperature, it would be a worthwhile endeavor to explore the interfacial magnetism and EB effect in WSe2/MoS2 and TiSe2/MoS2 heterostructures.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-dimensional van der Waals magnetic heterostructure formed by stacking a monolayer (or few-layer) VSe2 film on a MoS2 film. In this system, magnetic moments arise from (i) the V atoms of VSe2 and (ii) defect-induced local moments associated with Se vacancies in VSe2 and with Mo- or S-vacancies in MoS2. Because VSe2 and MoS2 have different work functions, contact between them produces interfacial charge redistribution and a Schottky-type barrier, modifying the local carrier density (in particular electron accumulation in the VSe2 layer). The exchange-bias (EB) effect of the heterostructure is characterized by a horizontal shift H_EB of the magnetic hysteresis loop along the field axis after field cooling.

Develop a microscopic model and answer the following questions:

(a) Determine the nature (sign, magnitude, and spatial range) of the magnetic exchange coupling at the VSe2/MoS2 interface between V-atom spins, Se-vacancy-induced spins in VSe2, and the Mo- or S-vacancy-induced spins in MoS2, and identify which of these couplings dominantly produces the EB effect.

(b) Quantitatively assess whether work-function-driven interfacial charge transfer and the resulting Schottky barrier enhance the ferromagnetism of the VSe2 layer and consequently increase H_EB; in particular, derive the dependence of H_EB on the amount of transferred charge per interfacial unit cell.

(c) Predict how H_EB depends on (i) the thickness of the MoS2 layer down to the monolayer limit, (ii) the Se-vacancy concentration in VSe2 (which controls the VSe2 net magnetization), and (iii) replacement of VSe2 by other defect-magnetic transition-metal dichalcogenides such as WSe2 or TiSe2.

Provide either a closed-form prediction or a numerically validated model (e.g., from first-principles plus a microscopic spin Hamiltonian) for each of (a)–(c).
artifact.status_search_result: No publication appears to have provided a complete microscopic answer to these questions for VSe2/MoS2 heterostructures. Recent works (2022–2025) discuss exchange bias and interfacial magnetism in 2D vdW heterostructures and confirm tunability of VSe2 magnetism via Se vacancies, but a unified description of the V/defect-spin interfacial coupling, Schottky-driven EB enhancement, and systematic dependence on MoS2 thickness or substitution by WSe2/TiSe2 has not been established. The problem is therefore considered open.
